==Journal==
{{Journal entry|Little is known about the great necromancer, Abraxus, a fact he finds deeply frustrating. In his youth he sought secrets forbidden to others and he wandered the Whispering Swamps of Brynmoor in search of secrets that others dared not know. The swamp was ancient and haunted, so the legends went, and there was a magic to it that was different to any other part of Ashenfall. He explored vaults, caves and battled goblins in the mists, but never found the power that his youth demanded. Until one day, he found the smoke that promised him the power he so desperately craved.

From there his history is clouded, obscured just as the mist obscured the swamps. He founded a small order of necromancers in Fellhollow and took advantage of the chaos when the Withering began. He sought to bind the souls of the dead into his service, gaining power just as Imaru gained hers from the consumption of the fallen.

But Abraxus was no dragon, and so frustratingly mortal. A single hoplite spear is all it took to end his life, he would have been embarrassed if he felt it had mattered. As a spirit he lost a lot of things we take for granted, sensation, corporeality, and many of the emotions that everyone else enjoys. Yet, in exchange, he was given the most precious gift of all – time. Time to contemplate. Time to scheme. Time to think about what really matters, in the grand scheme of it all, and he has found his answer.

His ring, imbued with his dark power, offers no value to him any more. So he bequeaths it to you. In time, perhaps, it may help you become a mage strong enough to earn his respect. Well, a small fraction of it, at least. 
}}

The '''abyssal whip''' is a [[power level]] 4 one-handed [[masterwork]] melee weapon that can be created at a [[blacksmith's bench]]. The recipe can be acquired from the [[Kletterbuja Kara]] [[vault]] by interacting with a dragonkin statue clutching a blue orb, and hidden within a concealed alcove on the upper floor, near the ledge-jumping path, provided players have the [[abyssal spine]] that is dropped by an [[abyssal demon]] in the player's inventory. It can be ascended at a [[mystic forge]] with [[ascension core]]s.

Its special attack is abyssal snare, which costs 20 [[stamina]] and takes 0.8s to cast and a 1.15s delay afterwards which sends out a slow-moving purple projectile that homes in on nearby enemies and explodes in a small radius after colliding with an enemy, wall, or after about 2 seconds, and knocks down most foes for roughly 3 seconds. Performing any action before it has impacted a target will cause it to disappear. It cannot travel up or down ledges, but the explosion can still affect foes close to the ledge where it collided. The special attack is unaffected by both [[Enchant Weapon: Fire]] and [[Enchant Weapon: Air]].

[[File:Abyssal Whip Special Attack Animation.gif|alt=Abyssal Whip Special Attack Animation|thumb|Abyssal Whip Special Attack Animation]]

This weapon's [[special effect]] is that regular attacks also build up [[bleed]], and after five rapid hits, will proc 28 damage at [[power level]] 4 and 40 damage at [[power level]] 7, despite only listing 25 for each. As this weapon deals slash damage, compared to swords, it attacks are slightly slower but slightly harder, however its forward lunge distance is much shorter, and since enemies are knocked back significantly by most attacks, they will be often be knocked out of this weapon's combos. It also does not have increased block without a shield compared to other similar weapons.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
[[Abyssal demon]]s are foul beasts. A single specimen can massacre a village before the warning bell can even sound. Crafting a weapon from their remains symbolises triumph against adversity or, perhaps, just hubris in its purest form.

Infused with the hate of the demon, each whip crack generates unbearable pain. Victims find themselves overcome with suffering as the agony seeps into the wounds the whips leave behind.

It is said that the whip even feeds on that misery, growing stronger with each strike, each life taken. The hate imbues the weapon with a desire to inflict more pain, and it grows stronger each time such a wish is granted. Or, so the legends say.

Only one [[wild knight]] has ever chosen to wield the whip in vengeance against a demon for a fallen sibling. Her name is dust in the wind of history, but there are still creatures that hide in the shadows, afraid of the crack of her whip.

== Trivia ==

* In both ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'' and ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}, adamant bar is created in different numbers.''
** In ''RuneScape,'' the bar is created using 1 adamantite ore and 1 {{RSL|Luminite|luminite}} (the replacement to coal).
*** In ''RuneScape''<nowiki/>'s lore, adamantite is hard to form into an bar, even with coal. A replacement was found, luminite, which made it easier to turn the ore into a bar. As such, it is known to be smelt without luminite, but it would require very high temperature, which explains it needing a blast furnace.
** In ''Old School RuneScape'', the bar is created needing 1 adamantite and 6 coals.

== Journal ==
{{Journal entry|
The first adamant mace was not, as you might expect, used for battle. Rather it was a rolling pin used by the ancient matriarch known only as The Crone – a name she chose for herself, thinking it quite funny.

Her baking skills were so dire, that whatever she produced had the consistency of iron and was more durable than steel. So, she required a tool strong enough to fight back against her sturdy pastries. She commissioned a rolling pin of adamant metal, and she used it with great zeal to beat her baked goods into submission.

Though teeth would still shatter against her scones, there was an artistry there that none could deny. So it was that more people would create adamant rolling pins, until an angry chef beat her rude husband to death with it, and the first true adamant mace was born.

After that, Moon Garou would still favour an adamant rolling pin, but many a warrior would bring a mace into battle, just in case they were forced to face up against the crone’s pastries. Which happened more often than is reasonably explainable.
}}

As [[Malgo]] and his expedition headed into the deserts of Ashenfall, they found wonderous new ores, materials and treasures that promised to expand their knowledge and understanding by leagues. They also found [[Karibdos]], the devourer.

It was a great beast that lay within the sands; some dread creature that should never have existed. It was buried beneath the region, massive and hungry and, as the expedition approached, it opened wide its maw and attempted to swallow the entire group whole.

With quick thinking and forgotten spells, Malgo summoned vines for the expedition members to grasp. Many failed and were consumed by the great vortex in the sand that was Karibdos.

Though they struck back, their arrows and spells were too weak to pierce its hide and Karibdos simply returned to its slumber, waiting for the expedition to cross its path again.}}

A little know tradition among Moon Garou blacksmiths, is to gather up all the bits of scrap metal from their workshops and create from them little figurines. They then sit beneath the shade somewhere, with various paints and turn these tiny creations into little pieces of art.

That was, until, Thraag learned of the game. Thraag was a blacksmith only so much in that he liked seeing metal melt. Something about the glow, the heat and the sheer sturdiness of the cooling metal, filled him with a sense of pride he never put into his personal hygiene.

Reeking like some unholy nightmare, Thraag was never invited to the gatherings of other blacksmiths, and over time the slight of being shunned festered within him, slowly mutating into something nasty.

He crafted a great hammer of pure adamant, sturdier and heavier then any hammer ever crafted before and he brought said hammer to the blacksmith gathering. There are few sights quite so tragic as grown blacksmiths weeping over smashed figurines.

It certainly did nothing to improve Thraag’s social standing.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
The Wild Knights knew the dangers of missing their target. If an arrow did not slay its target quickly, then too soon would the quarry either escape, or, worse, gather friends. Wolf packs could easily tear a small group of Knights to pieces if not dealt with fast.

This includes the sweeping breath attack that all [[dragon]]s perform, as well as the poison spit from [[green dragon]]s, the spinning fire from [[Imaru]], the lightning ball from [[blue dragon]]s, and the fireball from [[red dragon]]s and [[Fuzan]]. This does not include any ground-based effects like [[Velgar]]'s poison breath/barrage and earth spikes, [[Imaru]]'s [[wither]] projectiles and spikes, and [[Fuzan]]'s lava floor. Notably, despite not being listed, this special effect is also present on the [[dragonblight shield]] and [[dragoncurse shield]] but not on the [[dragonfire shield]]. All of that being said, [[Tempest Shield]] will block all incoming damage (excluding any ground-based attacks), including the projectiles and spikes that weren't blockable even with the [[special effect]], and that is available even with two-handed weapons. Otherwise, all [[vestige]] and [[masterwork]] [[shields]] can be ascended to the highest [[power level]] and will have the same block value, with the exception of the [[fallen hoplite's aspis]] which has 3 more and the [[toktz-ket-xil]] which has 6 less. Therefore, the optimal [[shield]] choice will come down to their [[special effects]], and this [[shield]] may often be chosen as it can block dragonfire but will not interfere with staggers caused by parries, unlike the other dragon shields. Wizards always push themselves too far. They compete academically with anything that moves, insisting on demonstrating their intellectual superior over everyone around them. Their intelligence is a glittering brooch that must be seen by everyone.

Academia creates a sort of stress that could be bottled and weaponised, only to be banned by conventions around the world for its cruelty. Yet, a wizard does it to themselves, pushing and pushing beyond the limits of the human condition.

Inevitably they turn to external solutions, and this particular mixture has pushed many a mage past academic burnout just long enough to get by. Somehow it makes magic flow easier, spells cast stronger than before, and the wizard is capable of feats they might never have achieved before.

It's not entirely clear why a staff helps channel magic. Druids would claim that it was because they were working with nature, aligning the magic spell through the plant's systems. Members of the Wizard's Guild argued that it wasn't that the wood itself was special but that they worked as a focus, helping to channel the mind of the wizard.

The inclusion of rune essence in a staff's design is a testament to the meticulous craftsmanship and artistry involved. This essence, often crushed into a fine powder and dispersed throughout the wood's careful grooves, creates a magical circulatory system within the staff. In this way, the staff becomes a living entity, with the wizard as its beating heart, channelling power through its veins to unleash upon foes. 

A staff is rarely helpful for less violent magic. They are brute force weapons, where magic is forced into elemental blasts, obliterating the target. More subtle spells rely on the caster's will and are powered directly by their magical skill.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Ava is the apprentice to Dr Oddenstein, an eccentric scientist who lives in Draynor Manor, and a skilled inventor in her own right. She whiles away her limited free time by studying the lesser-known field of necroballistics, and creating strange and wonderful gizmos to further her studies.

Perhaps her proudest achievement, is the invention of the attractor. By harnessing the energies of an undead chicken to the harmonic frequencies of a common bar magnet, her device can snatch grounded projectiles and bring them back to the quiver before they can be lost. This money saving experiment is not only great for hunters, but for anyone looking for an excuse to fill their enemies full of sharp sticks of wood.

Always the generous sort, but one with little head for marketing, Ava has decided to pass on her genius invention to others. Rather than publishing a paper, or passing the methodology onto the Varrock library, she has instead written the instructions in a bottle and sent it adrift in the ocean for anyone to find. Fate, she believes, will draw it to where it is meant to go. Like magnets, probably.
}}

'''Milliburn Rasmodel''', also known as '''Lord Rasmodel''', and the '''Black Knight Titan''' is a [[power level]] 6 [[boss]] [[Monsters|monster]], released with [[Dowdun Reach]]. He is the old commander of the [[Black Knights]] within Dowdun Reach, who was resurrected by the [[Avisk|Dreaming Stone]], and guards the passageway to the [[Umbral Sands]].

==History==
Milliburn was the eldest son of the Rasmodels' house, a noble house from the mainland, who worshipped [[Saradomin]] before rebelling against him. When the [[Children of Shadows]] became allied with the family, Milliburn's brother would play pranks on the members who became bodyguards to the nobles. When his father died, he became the head of the house. During his rule, he kept having dreams and visions, which eventually led him to believe that he needed to form the Shadow Knights, believing [[Imaru]], [[Xikotal]], and [[Fellhollow]] itself could not be trusted. 

After reforming the Children of Shadows into the '''Black Knights''', Milliburn would continue to rule over Dowdun Reach. After the [[Dragon Rebellion]], when Kuldra ordered her dragons to lay waste to the inhabitants of [[Ashenfall]], the Black Knights were able to hold their own against the dragon attacks. Their defences were greatly strengthened thanks to the '''Dreaming Stone''', but it would sow whisper and madness in his and others' minds. After a period of time with the stone, which had caused distrust, Milliburn had decided to destroy it, finally being free of the madness. Before he could do anything else, his family, the Rasmodel house, would appear before him, telling him to rest, that they would take it from here. Now his body remains within the [[Black Knight's Fortress]], controlled by his insanity and unknowingly guarding the way to [[Umbral Sands]].

==Journal==
{{journal entry|The Dreaming Stone had been shattered.

Lord Rasmodel, on his knees, heard no voices. For the first time in too, too long, he could hear his own breath. His heart played a welcome beat. For decades, he had felt like he floated above the world. Now he was part of it again.

Footsteps. Lord Rasmodel lifted his head wearily. Who would interrupt this moment?

Tinging around him was his family. The Rasmodels. They were all there - all the ones he knew, and loved and had met. They were dressed as the finest nobility, the Rasmodels at their height. They had regained their standing - the name meant something again.

His father knelt down and lifted Lord Rasmodel's bloody chin. Their eyes met. " Rest," his father said. "We will take it from here."

Milliburn Rasmodel, twenty-fifth Lord of Rasmodel, took his retirement.
}}

{{Journal entry|The stranger the wood, the more powerful the magic. It’s uncertain why this is, but it’s been true since magic was first discovered. When used as a tool for destructive magic, [[Garou Druids|garou druids]] learned the power of [[blightwood]]. 

[[Ashien]], a legendary druid among the [[Garou (race)|garou]], was among the first to wield such a weapon. As the story goes, they were wandering the swamps when the goddess [[Lougrim]] came to her in a vision and gave her a quest. Ashien was to journey deep into the swamps and do battle with a demon that dwelled{{sic|supposed to be dwelt}} within. 

They found the demon; it emerged out of the fog with a chilling screech and destroyed their staff with a single swing of its blade-like claw. In panic, Ashien blindly reached for the nearest weapon, the root of a swamp tree that had fallen in the mud. Through it, she channeled their will to survive and it burst free of the branch as a flash of lightning. 

The creature burned beneath Ashien’s gaze, vanishing back into the mists as if it never were. 

Since then, garou druids would favour blightwood when crafting a staff.}}

{{journal entry|
The [[Bloodblight Swamp|Bloodblight swamp]] was once a pleasant place. Golden fields of wheat, rustling in the breeze. Life here was simple yet fulfilling.

Until [[Velgar]] took it all away.

He fought the mighty god of war, [[Bandos]], and he should have lost. Dragons are powerful, and Velgar is stronger than most, but even in his most arrogant days he was no match for a god.

Yet, arrogance is not a mortal taint and the war god reeked of it. Bandos cast aside his wards. He refused to don his armour. The god pressed into the lair of the great dragon, and tried to wrestle him to the grave.

He nearly succeeded. Bandos wrapped his arms around the dragon’s serpentine neck and dug his fingernails beneath the scales. Velgar, in his writhing fury, called down a poison-filled rock from the heavens and cast it at Bandos, striking him in the temple. As the god reeled, he released Velgar, allowing the dragon to breathe a jet of [[anima]]-infused poison, at the unsteady god. Still wavering from the blow, Bandos breathed in the toxins and felt weakness for the first time in centuries.

A smart tactician, Bandos retreated. Better to face the shame of retreat, than risk the oblivion of death.

In his jubilant rage, Velgar spilled his blood on the once fertile plains, corrupting them with his hate-filled poison. The fields wilted. The crops blackened and then collapsed into venom.

This cloak, is reminder of that blighted day.
}}

The '''blurite crossbow''' is a [[power level]] 4 [[crossbow]] that can be crafted at a [[fletching bench]]. The recipe is learned after studying the [[azure metal contraption]] found in a [[chest]] in northwest [[Fractured Plains]]. It can be ascended at a [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension cores]].

Its [[special effect]] is -25% Reload Duration, making it reload faster than other crossbows. It also lists -25% [[durability]], but it has the same amount as an [[iron crossbow]].

The [[dorgeshuun crossbow]] can only fire [[bone bolts]], so if specifically wanting to fire metal or [[enchanted bolts]], this is one of the best options to do so. The [[shadow crossbow]]'s special effect is 15% increased damage to [[weakpoint]]s, which is a multiplicative modifier when considering weakpoints, 3/3 [[ranged armour]], and the [[amulet of glory]], but it fires slower than normal crossbows, making it much slower than this or the dorgeshuun crossbow. One of the benefits of crossbows is the flinch they cause on each hit, and the faster crossbows will do that more often.

==Journal==
{{journal entry|
For centuries{{sic|missing comma}} alchemists have yearned to create gold. To transmute base metals into something pure and shiny. While gold is the goal, there are other, stranger metals, along the way, and what could be more bizarre than a bar of purest blue.

Blurite is defined by its colour. It’s in the very name. Yet it offers no real magical, or alchemical value beyond other metals. Artistic, perhaps, it was favoured by poets, bards and{{sic|missing Oxford comma}} artisans of more eccentric tastes, but it still offered little in the way of superior weaponry.

That was until Gothren Actillian took a crack at it. He was an blacksmith{{sic|supposed to be "a blacksmith"}}, obsessed with the less desired metals and materials. He would hunt for hours in the darkest caverns for slivers of blue, ignoring glittering silver and gold. To him the metal was special, radiant and{{sic|missing Oxford comma}} beautiful. The hues generated a joy in him that he could not describe, and he longed to craft it into something befitting its splendour. He was delighted when he found the ore glittering away in a hidden dragonkin vault in Ghornfell's central region.

He was never any good with a sword, and his magical prowess wouldn’t frighten a kebbit. Yet crossbows, those he could wield. He was a skilled marksman, and could knock an apple from a chinchompa’s head before it exploded.

The crossbow, blue as the ocean, caused much mockery from his companions, yet their mockery soon died as he speared a bolt through the heart of a dragon. Something all of their weapons had failed to do.

He was just disappointed that the dragon’s scales were green and went searching for that ever elusive blue.
}}

The '''bow of Elidinis''' is a [[power level]] 7 [[masterwork]] [[longbow]] that can be crafted at a [[fletching bench]]. The recipe is received as a reward for completing the [[Mapping The Sands II]] quest. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension cores]].

Its first [[special effect]] is Blessing of Elidinis, which makes [[arrows]] also deal [[water magic]] damage in addition to [[ranged]] damage. Kills with water magic have a chance to drop [[water orb]]s that provide some [[health]] and a little [[hydration]] when picked up. Its special action is Lunar Rain, which costs 6 [[stamina]] and deals [[water magic]] damage over the targeted area for a short time. This is considered a [[Magic]] attack rather than a [[Ranged]] one, providing Magic [[XP]] and benefitting from the [[lesser magic potion]] and 3/3 magic armour's set effect increasing the chance of getting [[critical strike]]s instead of Ranged XP and weakpoint modifiers. However, its other special effect is Purity of the Moon, which is supposed to prevent the use of [[Ranged_weapons#Arrows_2|barbed, poisoned, and fire arrows]] when using this bow. However, this does not work, and all of those arrows can be fired from this weapon.

Similar to the [[zombie axe]], when using normal, barbed, or poisoned arrows, this weapon deals both ranged and water damage simultaneously. Unlike most other damage modifiers, this damage is additive, which means that attacking an enemy weak to one but resistant to the other will result in more damage done than expected, but less than an enemy neither weak nor resistant to either. However, when using fire arrows, the water damage is replaced with fire. When comparing this bow to the [[hunter stagbow]] against [[KotHaar]] specifically, it deals slightly more, but the stagbow fires slightly faster. Therefore, when not using Astral Rain, in all other situations, the hunter stagbow is the ideal longbow to ascend.

The heart of [[Bramblemead Valley|Bramblemead]] village was never really the castle, which came much later to the party. It wasn’t the town hall. It wasn’t the druid huts. It was the windmill. Grain heaped by the village was brought here and milled down into flour. The flour became bread, pastry and batter, turning village meals into something that helped people to live, rather than simply survive.

Food, becomes a banner around which everyone can gather. To break bread with one’s enemy was a way to settle old scores, and forge new connections. More good has been done over the dinner table, than on any throne. Flour, turned Bramblemead from a settlement, into a thriving village.

When humanity fell, it was rats and goblins that claimed the heart of the village, though they had no use for the swirling sails.

To the goblins it was a place where food could be hidden. Supplies sealed up from rival tribes. For the rats, it was a restaurant full of goblin supplies that were never well sealed.

The sail no longer turns. But, perhaps, in the fullness of time, this village heart might beat again.

==Journal==
{{journal entry|
The members of the Wild Knights who trained with melee weapons, generally found themselves the victors in friendly sparring matches against their companions. The reasoning was simple – shields. A shield could turn aside blade, arrow and spell, with equal skill{{sic|missing Oxford comma}} and it left their enemy vulnerable to counterattack. This sense of superiority began to change from friendly competition, into a sense of smugness capable of souring many friendships.

Roliker Hallister was particularly obnoxious. His skill with sword and shield was admittedly impressive. At the age of twenty{{sic|missing comma}} he could best even some of the commanders of the Wild Knights in single combat. Healthy pride twisted into smug egoism, which then rotted down into unpleasant superiority. He was rude. He was dismissive. He was pretty much an obnoxious nightmare to be around.

Which is why he was very surprised by the bolt in his shoulder, and why no one else seemed too inclined to help him out. Vanida Mox was a skilled archer and inventor. She was quick to learn, quick to study{{sic|missing Oxford comma}} and she had the enviable ability to see when something was wrong and work to find a solution. Popular with the other knights, because she would work with them, share accolades, and stand for what the order truly meant – a barrier between the world and the wild.

As Roliker’s ego grew and grew, she realised that the archers in the order were at a significant disadvantage in close combat. At range, they were obviously superior, but as all the sparring matches were held in the courtyard, there was precious little distance available. So she began working on a device that would deliver the power of an arrow{{sic|missing comma}} but allowing one hand free to hold a shield.

It was very effective.

She named it a “cross-bow”, because she was very {{sic|missing comma}}very angry when she unloaded it into the cloud of smugness known as Roliker. Later{{sic|missing comma}} that name would be attributes{{sic|supposed to be "attributed"}} to the mechanical structure of the device, but now you know better.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|Bronze is a common enough alloy, a combination of copper and tin. Durable, defiant, and deadly in the right hands. For [[Mia Larsdottir]], it was a bronze dagger that pierced her heart, cutting her life short at the age of twenty-one. 

As the first of the [[Amalgamated]], she had never expected to reach any of the milestones traditionally followed by her peers. She did not expect to be married and she never let herself dream of being a mother. She thought, perhaps, that she might be allowed to carve a quiet little place for herself, somewhere with room for cats. 

But a bronze dagger stole that dream from her. 

Her killer was never brought to justice, though there were rumours about who they were. Her father was the chief suspect, ashamed as he was to bring the first of the unnatural Amalgamated into the world. He denied it, of course, but he never held a funeral for her. Instead, her body was left in the forest, where nature might put her at peace.}}

==Journal==
{{journal entry|
While heavier than other materials, there’s little argument that a bronze shield is a superior defence to wood and leather materials. The metal turns aside almost any blow, protecting the wielder behind its mass. 

Even the [[Wild Knights]], who usually shunned metal weapons, would don bronze shields into battle. Their philosophy was that a life is worth more than a principle. 

Before the peace treaty with their goddess, [[Lougrim]], the [[Garou (race)|garou]] would often get into conflict with travelling villagers. They saw the humans as prey, willfully intruding on their land and therefore consenting to be hunted. The humans, of course, saw things differently. 

Garou weapons were powerful and delivered by creatures of unnatural strength. Yet bronze would defend against these attacks, and it gave the garou pause, for they had yet to battle foe with such intriguing technology. Battles that would previously have been a slaughter became skirmishes as the garou tested their might against these new bronze defences. 

This comparative peace did not last long. 
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|Legend has it that when the first sword was forged, [[Guthix]] wept. Given that Guthix commissioned warriors and soldiers and, at times, encouraged war, this is perhaps not a truthful statement. Yet, the sword is a weapon with a singular purpose: to end the life of another. Of course, this is true of all weapons, but none are as iconic as the blade.

Children would play in the street, striking one another with wooden blades rather than clubs or daggers. They would pretend to be knights rather than brigands or priests. To wield a blade was a sign of bravery. To draw a sword was the hero's stance.

War shatters all childhood dreams.

Nothing removes the nonsense of chivalry more efficiently than seeing the life leaving the eyes of a terrified foe. A sword puts the wielder in that moment, forcing them to face that which they destroy; to understand that there are no such things as heroes:{{sic|supposed to be a semicolon}} only warrior against warrior and the knowledge that one will fall.}}

[[Doric]] would be the first person to praise the simple hammer. It is a large solid chunk of metal attached to a long haft, allowing the weapon to benefit from the unmistakable might of physics. Weight and speed are a terrifying combination. 

[[Dwarves]], in particular, favour this weapon. They feel it speaks to their long-held desire to form metal by pounding it into shape by sheer strength alone. They apply the same logic to their enemies, beating them into a shape that the dwarves feel suits their enemies better.

==Journal==
{{journal entry|
In the early days of Brynmoor, back when it was rather more active than it is now, there were artisans of great skill who would gather in secret to weave tapestries of such aesthetic wonder that they could never be shown.

Some, depicted the power of Saradomin. Others, the beneficence of Guthix, or the wickedness of Zamorak. A few depicted scenes of natural beauty, such as the green forests, the undulating dunes of the desert of the sharp peaks of the mountains.

One, depicted something far more sinister. It depicted the future. Suizzy was best known for their embroidery of owls, adding them as secret filigree to all of their pieces. Yet, on one fateful night of clandestine sewing, they were overcome by a vision so terrible, that they had to depict it in fabric.

A dragon, rising from the flames of the underworld and dragging with it a terrible withering curse that would claim all life in the region. It was a cursed thing. A terrible sight. Yet, the other crafters were drawn to its strange and sinister beauty.

It was sealed away, deep within the soil. Lost for centuries. Until a new group of adventurers, accidentally found a way to bring it to the light.
}}

==Trivia==
* The design of the cape came from ''Suizzy'' as their submission for the Fellhollow Cape Contest, hosted on the ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' official Discord channel.

== Journal ==
{{Journal entry|
The mind is a powerful thing. Thought can shape reality; intention turns to impulse, which moves muscle and bone, which in turn can shatter stone. The Aughra were fascinated by such power and sought more and more ways to harness it.

For Avisk, who was determined to force his will on all living beings, it was a myriad collection of tools in one, squishy, vessel. Dreams and nightmares were an especially fascinating study. Dreams, like thoughts, can shape reality. A child dreams of the stars and goes in search of the tallest trees, the highest mountains, anything to help him get closer to those twinkling baubles.

The elderly dream of their youth and regret decisions made decades in the past. Entire lifespans can exist in moments. Avisk yearned to harness that power.

When he crafted the crucibles, he distilled nightmares down to their purest forms. Each one forged from archetypes shared across countless species. Yet what nightmare is stronger then when friends become foes, when trust turns to betrayal. When we look into the eyes of our loved ones, what if it’s hatred that shines back?

This key is the concept of betrayal crystallised down and used to unlock the Nightmare Crucible. The beasts inside offer no loyalty, for in a world forged by betrayal they know that trust is nothing but a pleasant fiction.
}}

The '''crystal bow''' is a [[power level]] 3 [[masterwork]] [[shortbow]] that can be obtained (as well as its crafting recipe) as a reward from the [[Heartstrings]] quest. It can then be crafted at a [[fletching bench]]. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension cores]].

Its [[special effect|special attack]] is called '''Shattershot''', costing 43 [[stamina]] and shoots an area-of-effect cone of arrows a short distance that deals one third of the weapon's base damage to every target hit. Each target hit is stuck with crystal needles that explode after a short time for a set 50 damage. More needles can be stacked before the previous set explodes. This special attack does not require arrows to fire and can penetrate solid objects.

This weapon fires slightly slower than other shortbows despite dealing very similar damage when at the same power level, even when compared to the [[undead ranger's bow]] which is supposed to have increased damage as its special effect. This weapon has the same durability as the other ascendable shortbows, which makes the [[wild scout's shortbow]] with its 10% faster draw speed the ideal choice of shortbow to ascend if not using shattershot.

A Crystal Bow is not crafted but sung into existence. Harmonies are layered over one another to teach the weapon a story so that it might understand why it needs to be strong. Traditionally, the songs that are sung are of the plight of the elves, their loneliness without their goddess, and the many dangers they must face.

The shimmering substance they're made from is traditionally a shard of the elven goddess {{RSL|Seren}}, left behind when her crystal form shattered at the end of the {{RSL|Third Age}} {{RSL|God Wars}}.

This bow isn't of the same material, and the song is different, too. There's no divine essence in the crystal, no lament of the elves. Instead, it is sung memories of a lifetime together, distilled down into facets reflecting in the crystalline flaws. In the moonlight, those facets sparkle like tiny stars held within glass — moments of hardship, conflicts, happiness{{sic|missing serial comma}} and grief.

It is music as a weapon, with memory as its handle and sorrow as its string.
}}

==Trivia==
* Dihydrogen monoxide is the formal chemical name for water.
** The in-game journal entry and description for this item refer to the ironic use of the name "dihydrogen monoxide" instead of its commonplace name, water, to give the impression that this is a dangerous chemical. Often, it is accompanied by alarming descriptions of its properties, such as saying "this chemical causes suffocation" to describe the dangers of drowning in water, as a means of illustrating how such language can mislead the reader. This ironic usage highlights the importance of public education in science.

The '''dorgeshuun crossbow''' is a [[power level]] 5 [[crossbow]] that can be crafted at a [[fletching bench]]. The recipe is obtained from the quest [[Even More Restless Ghosts]]. It can be ascended at a [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension cores]].

Its [[special effect]] is a hidden -25% Reload Duration, making it reload faster than other crossbows. It also can only fire [[bone bolts]], which can similarly only be fired from this crossbow. Unlike other crossbows and bolts that split the damage between them, all of it is on the crossbow. This is to ensure that the weapon ascends correctly, and isn't forced to use weaker bolts than other crossbows. The bone bolts additionally build [[bleed]], and with three hits in a short time, deal 40 damage. This damage does not scale with power level.

Excluding the bleed damage from the bone bolts, this weapon has the same base damage, reload speed, and durability as the [[blurite crossbow]] at similar power levels. With that in mind, the choice comes down to what bolts are desired, particularly [[enchanted bolts]], as the difference is entirely down to their effects. Currently, there are no [[enchanted adamant bolts]], therefore this weapon and its bone bolts take the cake at power level 7. The [[shadow crossbow]] is a notable mention as it can squeeze more damage out of enchanted bolts with +15% [[weakpoint]] damage, but it does so far slower than this or the blurite crossbow.

Its [[special effect]] is +15% [[critical strike]] chance, which equates to an average 1.0375x damage increase. It also lists -15% [[durability]], but it has the same amount of [[durability]] and does not deplete faster than the [[iron dagger]]. 

Although [[keris]] has 2 higher max hit at [[power level]] 7, this dagger when ascended has the same stats as the [[wolfbane dagger]], and so when not attacking either [[kalphite]]s or [[wolf|wolves]], this is the ideal one-handed stabbing weapon to ascend.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Viika was never fond of creating dragons, they thought the process was cruel and unbecoming. When an egg was laid, Viika saw in that moment both the egg and the dragon it would become. They saw past and presence{{sic|supposed to be present}} at the same time, and they grieved the creature before it had even hatched.

They pleaded with their sibling, and with the other Dragonkin, to change their treatment of the beasts. But Viika’s curse, like so many Seers, was to be ignored by their kindred.

A rare egg hatched once, containing a dragon with white scales like pearls. The dragon was infused with magic and possessing{{sic|supposed to be possessed}} a power capable of travelling to other worlds, where she might have lived a happier life. But Viika wept, for they knew she would manage no such ending.

Viika kept the hatchling company. Treated them like their dearest friend, and held them softly when Lacrussa’s need for knowledge, took the dragon’s last breath.

The Seer kept only a single keepsake – a blade carved from the tooth of their white-scaled friend. A dagger capable of terrible damage, but as fragile as the friendship that it reminded them of.
}}

The '''dragoncurse shield''' is a [[power level]] 5 [[masterwork]] [[shield]] that is obtained from the [[Withering Heights reward pack]] by completing [[Withering Heights]]. It can be crafted at a [[blacksmith's bench]] after obtaining an [[undead draconic visage]] from the same pack or from turning in [[Imaru's head]] to [[Death (Grim Reaper)|Death]] afterwards, although it will require another [[anti-dragon shield]]. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension core]]s.

Its [[special effect]] causes a spectral dragon claw to rise from the ground and deal 25 damage<ref>Note that there are no damage numbers for this effect</ref> to and pull enemies slightly away from the player. Unlike the [[dragonblight shield]], the effect does not scale with [[power level]]. It has a 20 second internal cooldown. This damage will interrupt a stagger caused by a parry. Despite not being listed, this [[shield]] also has Dragon Breath Resistance, the [[special effect]] of the [[anti-dragon shield]], which provides the ability to block [[dragon]] fire.

As long as the target is not immune to [[poison]] (like [[green dragon]]s) and [[poison]] is not being applied from another source (like [[Venomous Trapper]], poisoned arrows, or [[weapon poison]]), then the [[dragonblight shield]]'s effect is better because the damage scales with [[power level]], dealing more total damage over time, and it doesn't interrupt staggers. That being said, [[fallen hoplite's aspis]] will also have more block value and [[toktz-ket-xil]] will have increased melee crit damage after a parry, but reduced block value.

The '''dragonfire shield''' is a [[power level]] 7 [[masterwork]] [[shield]] that is obtained from the [[Icthlarin's Little Helper reward pack]] by completing [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]]. It can be crafted at a [[blacksmith's bench]] after obtaining a [[smouldering draconic visage]] from the same pack<ref>This is missing from the pack, a known bug.</ref> or from turning in [[Fuzan's head]] to [[Icthlarin]] afterwards, although it will require yet another [[anti-dragon shield]]. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension cores]].

Its [[special effect]] launches a burst of lava forwards on a [[parry]], dealing 25 damage<ref>Note that there are no damage numbers for this effect.</ref> and causes [[Burning]] on nearby enemies, which deals 11 damage per second for 5 seconds for a total of 55 Burning damage. This effect does not have a cooldown. This damage will interrupt a stagger caused by a parry. Unlike the [[dragonblight shield]] and [[dragoncurse shield]], this shield does not currently have the anti-dragon shield's special effect Dragon Breath Resistance.

This shield has an excellent synergy with the [[fire cape]], which restores [[stamina]] when defeating Burning targets with [[Attack|melee]] attacks. Unfortunately, the fire cape and [[Enchant Weapon: Fire]] are just as good at causing Burning damage. [[Fire magic]] and [[fire arrows]] are also a common source of damage in a multiplayer setting that wouldn't stack, not to mention several enemies are resistant to Burning (like the knights and mages of [[Dowdun Reach]]) or immune to [[fire]] completely (like the [[KotHaar]]). The [[toktz-ket-xil]]'s increased melee damage after a parry (which does not interrupt a stagger) may still be more valuable.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Fuzan was the youngest of Kuldra’s offspring, yet one of her most violent. As a child he was overcome with a curiosity infused with childlike cruelty. When Kuldra gifted him with the flames, stolen from the Dragonkin’s Harmonic Resonator, it did nothing to temper that childlike need to discover and destroy.

The fires within him were a delight to wield and he grew more and more focused on their flickering flames, one day glancing through them to worlds of cinders that lay beyond. In the embers he heard a whisper, and as he listened it turned into a promise and a proclamation. A voice of true divinity, far surpassing the power of his mother’s dimmed spark.

She was a queen of worlds far beyond this one, each of them shining beacons in the dark twilight of the heavens and Fuzan was enraptured. Through her instruction he learned to mark others with his seal, sharing some of his power with them, and in turn, some of hers.

Now, with his destruction, you wield the flames yourself. A shield protecting you from her manipulation. Yet, should you stare too closely at the flames that burn within this shield, you might find yourself blinded by divine radiance.
}}

{{journal entry|
For a short time, a necromancer arrived on [[Ashenfall]]. She had found her way here by boat, fleeing pirates who wanted revenge for her misdeeds. Her skills were limited; she could not raise undead legions, but she had a knack for controlling simple fangs and bones. 

She fled into the forests – pirates having found Ashenfall and hunting her down – where she would unleash fang arrows against her foes in the hope of stopping their chase. It didn’t work. Broken, lost and without hope, she prepared herself for death. 

But death never came for her. 

Instead, a [[Wild Knight]], who wore a mask made from the skull of a wolf, rescued her. He pushed back her assailants and brought her to safety. Their fellowship after that was unbreakable, though no bond of romance flowed between them. She made the arrows, he fired the bow, and together, they feasted on their victories and kept the woods safe from unwanted intrusion. 

Even now, there are signs of their friendship. Hidden across the forest, miniature carvings of a wolf skull and a bat can be found in places that meant something to them.  
}}

==Journal==
{{journal entry|
[[Fellhollow]] could have been a new utopia, were it not for the cruelty of the [[Kuldra|godeater]]. Imaru and [[Xikotal]] adored their human neighbours and dreamed of a society where both dragon and human could thrive together in peace.

Now the land, like that dream, has broken. A hateful hunger from beyond the grave has consumed all the life, love and joy in the land. The dead roam desperately seeking to tear the tiniest threads of life from any living thing that crosses their path, and the afterlife itself, here, is poisoned by Imaru’s grief.

Yet, once, long ago, this land was beautiful. A myriad of colours danced in the breeze, the anima twist turning the region into a kaleidoscopic wonder. The now ruined streets were once filled with laughter, joy and song. And the dragons danced across the skies in loved-laced poetry.

This cape is a burieal{{sic|misspelled burial}} shroud for a world that could have been.
}}

==Journal==
{{journal entry|
[[Brakka]]’s hubris was a marvel to behold, perhaps more impressive than any monument of his construction. When [[Rasthin]] shared with him the elemental power she had wrung from [[Ashenfall]]’s mysterious vents, Brakka became a master of the earth itself.

With the power to shape stone and soil, by will alone, Brakka could have created great villages. He could have constructed aqueducts and watermills that could brought Ashenfall into a new, golden age. Instead, he made a tower.

A single tower that rose as far as the eye could see. Forged through his own power, and the blood, sweat and tears of [[Garou (race)|garou]] slaves. It is, perhaps, fitting, that this is where he died. [[Kuldra]], the godeater, crushed him beneath her great claw and feasted on his [[anima]]-rich soul. Stealing Brakka’s power for herself.

She gifted [[Velgar]], her most trusted general, with the elemental mastery of the fallen Nodon architect, and, to mock the [[dragonkin (race)|dragonkin]] further, Velgar took Brakka’s monument as his new lair.

Now the tower stands for all to see, as a reminder of dragonkin hubris, and rightfully deserves its new moniker; Brakka’s folly.
}}

The '''goblin "Swingslash"''' is a [[power level]] 2 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a [[crafting table]]. The recipe is learned by consuming [[a cruel goblin blade]], received as a random drop from a [[goblin pack]]; the drop chance for this vestige is 2%.

Despite having slash in the name, this weapon deals crush damage and uses the mace attack style. It has slightly higher base damage but the same durability as the [[bone club]], despite listing a [[special effect]] of -15% [[durability]].

It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension core]]s, but the base damage doesn't scale properly: the [[power level]] 2 [[goblin "swingslash"]] has 11-12% higher base damage than the [[power level]] 2 [[bone club]]'s 26 - 46, but the [[power level]] 7 [[goblin "swingslash"]] only has ~1% higher base damage than the [[power level]] 7 [[adamant mace]]'s 114 - 202).

While metal may be the preferred choice of weapon makers, the Granite Maul stands as a testament to the raw power of stone. This legendary weapon, revered among hammer wielders, is nothing more than a massive, heavy stone affixed to a stick. Yet, in the hands of a skilled wielder, it becomes a force of unparalleled destruction.

It was developed by ancient dwarves long ago, after one dwarf got fed up with the rock hammer he was using to fight a nest of gargoyles. In frustration, one dwarf took the biggest hunk of granite he could find and turned it into a legend.

{{Infobox Item |name = Grieving Moonstaff |image = Grieving Moonstaff.png |release = 15 April 2025 |update = RuneScape: Dragonwilds is out! |item_type = Magic Weapon |weight = 15.0 |repaircost = 1 [[oak logs]] |description = This staff is dedicated to Lougrim, the fallen Garou goddess of the Moon. }} The '''grieving moonstaff''' is a [[power level]] 3 [[staff]] that can be crafted at a [[mystic forge]]. The recipe is unlocked after studying [[a mysterious crescent carving]], which can be dropped by [[garou druid]]s with a 2/100 drop chance. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using [[ascension cores]]. Its [[special effect]] is -15% [[critical strike]] chance, which alongside its lower rune damage modifier at every [[power level]], makes this the weakest staff to ascend. For example, compare this to the [[draconic staff]]: That staff has +15% critical strike chance but has -15% [[durability]] to compensate. However, it has the same rune damage modifier as most other staffs at the same power level, while this staff has less, with no benefit to offset the reduced chance to crit. ==Stats== PL3= {{Infobox Weapon |power = 3 |specialeffect = -15% Crit Hit Chance |damagetype = Magic |attackstyle = Staff |runedamage = 2.6 |combo = 4 |durability = 1050 }} |-| PL4= {{Infobox Weapon |power = 4 |specialeffect = -15% Crit Hit Chance |damagetype = Magic |attackstyle = Staff |runedamage = 3.9 |combo = 4 |durability = 1050 }} |-| PL5= {{Infobox Weapon |power = 5 |specialeffect = -15% Crit Hit Chance |damagetype = Magic |attackstyle = Staff |runedamage = 5.2 |combo = 4 |durability = 1050 }} |-| PL6= {{Infobox Weapon |power = 6 |specialeffect = -15% Crit Hit Chance |damagetype = Magic |attackstyle = Staff |runedamage = 6.6 |combo = 4 |durability = 1050 }} |-| PL7= {{Infobox Weapon |power = 7 |specialeffect = -15% Crit Hit Chance |damagetype = Magic |attackstyle = Staff |runedamage = 8.1 |combo = 4 |durability = 1050 }} [[File:Grieving Moon Staff (Equipped).png|thumb|Grieving Moonstaff as seen when equipped to a player]] ==Recipe== {{Recipe |facility = Mystic Forge |recipe = A Mysterious Crescent Carving |skill = Artisan |skillxp = 40 |mat1 = Oak Logs |mat1qty = 8 |mat2 = Antler |mat2qty = 6 |mat3 = Animal Bone |mat3qty = 2 |output1 = Grieving Moonstaff |output1qty = 1 }} ===Recipe tree=== {{Crafting Tree|Grieving Moonstaff}} ==Journal== {{Journal entry|[[Lougrim]] was a moon deity, born to a cold world of soft silvers and silence. Her people lived lives of quiet contemplation, each moment spent wondering about the next. They were passive, soft spoken and sedentary, which drive Lougrim wild.

When a doorway to another world appeared and a grieving god wandered through it, Lougrim took the opportunity to run. To flee to another place, and live a life that she could endure.

History skips the next bit. Her closest allies have never learned what elevated her from her previous form to that of the goddess of the hunt, but whatever it is was profound enough to change her completely. She no longer resembled her silent kindred. She was quiet, yes, but in the way a tiger is moments before the kill. She is contemplative, true, but it was the stillness of a spider waiting for its prey.

When she found the [[Garou (race)|garou]], she knew she found her real kindred. They were violent, and deadly, and they yearned for the hunt. When she took her place as their goddess, she focused and refined them, creating hunters that were capable of felling almost any prey.

Yet still she kept the moon as her symbol, a reminder of her home and how far she has come since leaving it.

Now her priests bear the symbol, atop their staves and as the focus on their altars. They accept and revere [[Kuldra]] as their High Queen, yet they grieve the moon goddess that made them who they are today. }} ==Gallery== Grieving Moon Staff (concept art).png|Concept art for the grieving moonstaff ==Update history== {{UH| {{UL |type = update |date = [[29 July]] [[2026]] |ver = Eye on Ashenfall - 0.12.1 |update = This item can now be ascended to the highest available power level by using ascension cores at the mystic forge. }} {{UL |type = update |date = [[23 June]] [[2026]] |ver = Eye on Ashenfall - 0.12.0 |update = * Item is now created at the Mystic Forge, as the Smithing Anvil has been removed from the game. }} }} {{Staves}} {{Weapons}} {{Special Effects}}

[[Gahl]] was a [[Garou (race)|garou]] druid who lost everyone he knew. In the wars inflicted on his people by the other races of [[Ashenfall]], he grew jaded with the cruelty he saw all around him. This reached its peak when he found a garou village in ruins and goblins dancing and laughing as they threatened a newly born pup, in her crib.

The village is gone now, dragged beneath the soil. Gahl’s vengeance unleashed upon the goblins, erasing them from existence. He took the child as his own and raised her in a way alien to his people – he raised her with love.

She had no talent for magic, and could not learn his druid spells, so he taught her how to hunt with a bow, and she was a natural. [[Dahnu]], as he named her, made a bow out of the first deer she and her father had hunted and that bow became a symbol to all she encountered.

In time she would claim a king’s seat. Defeating the prior monarch with reason and wit. Charming him out of his power and offering her people another way.  

Her people thrived, making her father proud.

Until [[Velgar]] brought her reign to an end.
}}

The essence of an undead dragon, distilled down into a blade. What could go wrong?

This weapon is cold to the touch in ways far beyond chilling. Holding it feels as if you're out in the cold, with no shelter to protect you. Exposure in the palm of your hand.

Worse than the cold, is the hunger. This scimitar wants to cut, to stab, to slice and to maim. It wants to see your enemies bleed so that it can feast on their suffering. Imaru may be dead, but her hunter is eternal and you feel it infecting you with each swing of the blade.

}}

One mage created what she assumed was an auditory illusion, within an amulet, the intention being that when the wearer would try and cast a spell, the jewellery would play an annoying earworm tune, distracting the poor caster.

{{Journal entry|The [[Wild Knights]] used many tools and tricks in their hunts. Looking for any edge they might have against the untamed wilds of [[Ashenfall]]. {{Journal entry|
Iron turned the war against the garou more than some people would like to admit. They would claim superior training, tactics, and skills of their soldiers, but the truth is far simpler. Iron was strong and iron weapons were brutal.

Ranged weapons proved effective against the garou leadership, bound as they were by strict codes of honour. It is perhaps no surprise then, that there was a race to create weapons to challenge them.

The people of Brynmoor had learned of a Wild Knight invention, a weapon that would allow one to deliver powerful ranged attacks, whilst still allowing the bearer to wield a shield. They took this design, studied and refined it and then upgraded it to include the power of iron weapons.

Garou numbers dropped rapidly as a result, turning the war heavily against them. In their desperation, the garou turned to their goddess and she, in turn, sought allies with deadlier weapons still.

She was, after all, protecting humanity. Purging impurity. Ridding them all of the Amalgamated stain on their bloodlines. In her mind, she was doing the whole village a service. A worrying number of villagers agreed with her. 

As the wife of an elder, her sentence was light. An act of community service, doing what was already her job. She wasn’t imprisoned. She wasn’t executed. She wasn’t publicly condemned for her crime. She laughed off over a dozen murders with a cruel, smug smile. 

Although she carried an Iron Shield that weathered many attempted reprisals by Amalgamated enraged by the failure of justice, her real shield was the status she held. The wife of an elder, the blacksmith of the town, evidence incarnate that justice stopped when a victim was Amalgamated.

The '''keris''' is a [[power level]] 7 [[dagger]]. The recipe is learned from the [[corroded curved blade]], found in the vault in southwest Umbral Sands, in the chest after the [[kalphite queen]] boss fight. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension cores]].

Its [[special effect]] deals 25% increased damage against [[kalphite]]s, including [[kalphite worker]]s, [[kalphite soldier]]s, [[kalphite guardian]]s, and the [[kalphite queen]], but not to [[kalphite egg]]s. While upright, [[kalphite]]s are resistant to all forms of damage other than [[fire]], however, when knocked onto their backs either with enough damage or after a parry, they become weak to all forms of damage, increasing all other forms of damage by about a combined 85% (this weapon's first hit deals 50 damage to an upright [[kalphite]] and 92 damage when knocked down without a parry, while the [[adamant dagger]] deals 40 damage upright and 74 knocked down without a parry).

This weapon and the adamant dagger have slightly higher maximum hits compared to the [[dragonbone dagger]] and [[wolfbane dagger]] when ascended to [[power level]] 7 (59 - 150 vs. 59 - 152), however they excel in their respective areas: In [[Umbral Sands]], the player can be ambushed by [[kalphite]]s at any time, and the [[kalphite guardian]]s and [[kalphite queen]] can become immune to one of the three combat styles, so carrying this weapon out on the sands even when geared for either [[Magic]] or [[Ranged]] (especially since it only weighs 5.0) is worthwhile. Similarly, [[dire wolf|dire wolves]], [[dragonwolf|dragonwolves]], [[ghost wolf|ghost wolves]], and [[hellhound]]s will quickly close the gap, so the [[wolfbane dagger]] is a strong choice against them. In all other situations, the [[dragonbone dagger]]'s increased crit chance (even though it will be a lower bonus against those specific enemy types) will be best in all other situations.

A '''lodestone''' is a platform that allows the player to travel if another lodestone is placed elsewhere. When the first lodestone is built, the [[Lodestone (Inactive)|inactive lodestone]] in the [[Temple Woods|Temple]] starting area becomes active as well. Teleporting between two lodestones costs a varied amount of [[law rune]]s, depending on the distance of the target lodestone and the weight of the player. 

==Teleportation costs==
Teleporting between two lodestones costs an amount of law runes based on the distance between them and the amount of weight carried, with a minimum cost of one law rune. Note that the number shown on the lodestone map is calculated by the following:

<math>Law\, runes = (Distance\, to\, target\, lodestone\, \div 1000) \times (Total\, weight\, \div 1000)</math>

For example, teleporting 8000 meters (the length of 2000 [[square tile]]s) while weighing 400 kilograms would require <math>8 \times 0.4 = 3.2</math> law runes which rounds to 3.{{Fact}}

'''Lumber storage''' is a large [[storage]] container for storing lumber. Only logs and planks can be stored inside, and it can hold up to 48 item slots. If the lumber storage is placed within three metres of the receiving end of a sawmill, the sawmill will automatically deposit planks into it. Players can also build multiple sawmills with the sawing end within two metres, and have the processed planks go into the same storage. Players gain the ability to build lumber storage by reaching level 67 [[Woodcutting]], and gaining the feat lumber storage.

To craft or process an item without having the required items in their inventory, players must have the required items in their crate and check the "Linked" checkbox in the crate interface. This will allow players to craft up to 12 metres away from the crate.

{{Journal entry|
Garou magic is not born of runes, but of their connection to the moon, the stars and the spirits within them. Moon Garou shamans dance in the moonlight, with the glittering moon sprites swirling around them in mystical threads that help to reshape reality. Magic is sacred, spiritual and serene. Shamans wears these robes so that the tribe may know to call on them for spiritual aid, both magical and personal, as the shamans act as counsel as much as magician.

These robes are only given to a shaman after completing three mystic trials. The first is a trial of contemplation, where each applicant is given a complicated riddle to solve and three nights in which to do so. During that time they are allowed no forms of communication, and must rely purely on their ability to contemplate the words and arrive at a solution. The answers to the riddle are rarely set in stone: it is the interpretation that matters.

The second is a trial of compassion, and they are never warned of this one in advance. Indeed the trial may have happened before the applicant even entered into training. They could be tested at any point in their lives. It’s a simple trial: the applicant at some point finds someone in need and how they go about helping, or not helping them, is noted for the trial. This weeds out the cruel people pretending to be shamans, and encourages an attitude of compassion in potential applicants.

The final trial is the hardest of all, the trial of creativity. Here the applicants are given time to study magic, its forms, its methods and its malleability. To complete this trial, the applicant must create a new spell, enchantment or other form of magic, that has never been seen before. This trial has led to some of the most beautiful discoveries… and some of the most terrifying.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Before the master wand, there was a staff of such power that the mages of the wizard’s tower decided it was too dangerous to keep. They placed the staff in teleportation circle, scrambled the coordinates and hurled it through the Abyss to settle far away from Misthalin.

In truth, it should have ended in the depths of the sea, sinking down and down into the darkness, but something caught it instead.

A powerful elven mage had found their way to Ashenfall, and they had already indulged in powers darker than what their kin traditionally allowed. They felt the staff hurtling through the Abyss and used their unnatural sorcery to pull it to them, so that they might benefit from its power.

This elf and his retinue found their way to the Umbral Sands, where they challenged one of the Moon Garou’s mages to a magical duel, over some perceived slight or other. The battle was magnificent, power that shook the dunes and cast a great sandstorm into the skies. The garou was defeated, but not before her spells shattered the master’s staff.

In his arrogance he cast the remains aside and continued his journey into Ashenfall.  Moon Garou would find the remnants of the staff and found a way to recreate it. Weaker than the original, true, but still possessing a power that would make lesser mages tremble.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
In the Third Age on Ashenfall, mithril was incredibly desirable. It was only available in small quantities then, as its scarcity - perhaps inevitably - made it the fashion of the time. High-priests would incorporate it into their rosaries. Community leaders would wear it as brooches. It was rare enough that people would comment when they saw it. Ooh, Rosie's doing well for herself. That sort of thing. 

The idea of a mithril bar would have been mind-boggling to anyone in the Third Age. No matter their alignment, they'd have stabbed you in the belly and run away cackling with it. But here you are with an entire ingot. Take a moment and consider yourself a Third Age king.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
A mithril crossbow is the standard issue for any modern Black Knight. If you showed capability, then you might be promoted to Black Knight Sniper, and that came with the Black Sniper Crossbow. But for the average Black Knight, the crossbow was a long-kept friend.

The crossbow's main purpose was to stop demons in their tracks. The Zamorakian magi claimed to keep their demon hordes under control, but demons tested that claim.

The crossbow had other uses. Remove the bolt, rest the crossbow on the floor stock-upwards, and you had a stool. Sit on the floor and it was a headrest.

You could also waste time shooting ravens. Shooting the red, glowing ravens was an immediate dismissal, however. Alric demanded they were protected, for reasons that he never expanded on.
}}

And since 'elsewhere' would put it in the path of dragons, the Withering and Saradominists at various points on Ashenfall's timeline, you would have to surmise that no, Dowdun Reach would not exist.

There was a time, before the Withering, when a choice was made. The Children of Shadows became paranoid about the prospect of attack and betrayal. It did not seem to matter that they were guarded by dragons who manufactured peace. Dark whispers moved them to act.

Their lord, a man by the name of Rasmodel, prepared an edict whereby a faction would form. This would be the Shadow Knights, and the knights would enforce the will of Rasmodel.

An aspiring knight needs weapons and armour, which led to Rasmodel's choice. Were the knights to wear mithril, the metal that now freely flowed from the mines of Dowdun? It was strong enough, but mithril's value was in its perceived rarity. Or were they to import a different metal, one that would be costly and awkward to source - particularly for a force that wished to remain inconspicuous?

In the end, the choice was made for Rasmodel. The dragon, Xikotal, had a gift. In one claw, he had coal, in the other iron. He wanted to help the Zamorakians, to bring them an offering that might soften their determination to isolate. In the dragon's optimism, the gift would bring the Zamorakians into the wider Fellhollow community.

Rasmodel had his steel. He could outfit his new order. With the misguided dragon's help, he had his knights. They would ensure the rest of Fellhollow would keep their distance. }} ==Update history== {{UH| {{UL |type = update |date = [[23 June]] [[2026]] |ver = Eye on Ashenfall - 0.12.0 |update = * Item is now created at the Armour Bench, as the Smithing Anvil has been removed from the game. }} }} {{Mithril equipment}} {{Armour}}

== Ascension Upgrades ==
[[File:Mystic Forge Ascension.png|thumb|310x310px|The Ascension UI in the Mystic Forge.]]
Players can ascend their masterwork weapons and armour by collecting [[ascension core]]s through defeating enemies that drop ascension shards and creating them in the mystic forge or the cores directly through the [[Nightmare Crucible]]s. In order to start ascending weapons and armour, players will need at least 1 ascension core of the next power level available in either their inventory or chest along with a suitable item to ascend. This item must first be placed within the slot to ascend (it still stays in the inventory).

Ascending a masterwork weapon or armour piece consumes the core to bring it to the ''highest'' power level available to the player (<4 to 4, 4 to 5, 5 to 6, etc) and, if the player has multiple cores to reach the current highest power level in the game, the weapon or armour piece will require ascending ''twice'' to consume the cores needed to ascend to the highest power level in the game. It is worth noting here that weapons and armour that are already the ''highest'' power level ''cannot be ascended'' until a new major update.

Nightmare Crucible:
{{Stub}}

The '''Nightmare Crucible''' is a combat activity found within the [[Umbral Sands]] region of Ashenfall. It is meant to act akin to ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}''<nowiki/>'s {{RSL|Dominion Tower}} and ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}''<nowiki/>'s {{OSL|Nightmare Zone}} in where the [[player]] fights against all of the toughest enemies Ashenfall has to offer thus far.

To unlock a Nightmare Crucible, the player must use a corresponding item, called an Engram, whose title matches the Crucible of interest. An Engram only provides a single entry to a given Crucible - win or lose, the crucible will re-lock once the player enters it once. If the player dies while inside a Crucible, their [[gravestone]] will appear outside the crucible entrance.

The interior of Nightmare Crucibles are wide open, flat areas with almost no obstacles, save for the small Reward Pedestal in the center, and no safe spots for [[ranged]] or [[magic]] users. There is enough space to run around the arena in a circle and fight enemies from afar, but there is nowhere to hide. It is sometimes possible, depending on the player's positioning, to attract the attention of only a subset of the enemies in a given Crucible at a time.

The Longbow is every hunter’s friend. Capable of taking down prey over a greater range than the Shortbow, it has been the end of many a deer trying to flee through the woods. 

[[Bramblemead Valley|Bramblemead]] would host a thrilling archery tournament. The villagers would proudly bring their own Longbows, meticulously crafted by hand, and compete to take down cleverly hidden targets scattered across the village. It was a spectacle of skill and precision, with the only rule being that the target must be shootable from the open street. 

With the introduction of magic, the competition took on a whole new level of silliness. Participants conjured magical air currents that sent arrows astray – often into unsuspecting washing lines or pies cooling on windowsills – or they would playfully blast arrows out of the air with fire spells. 

However, this stopped after the [[Amalgamated]] archer, Derien, joined the game. Gifted with the element of air, his arrows curved gracefully with each shot, missing traps, tricks and deceptions. His victory earned the Amalgamated more jealousy, which led to the competition ending out of envious spite.

The villagers who proved their skills with an ash shortbow were brought into the forest by a [[Wild Knight]] instructor in search of more durable wood. The oak stood proud and tall in the forest, standing firm against the ebb of time. Villagers would gather the sturdiest branches that they found and bring them to a quiet place in the woods to begin carving their new bows. 

The Wild Knight would tell them that a good bow is more than just a weapon; it is an extension of oneself. They encouraged each villager to put a piece of themselves into the bow, a decoration on the handle or a poem carved into the wood. Whatever made the bow personal to them. 

This connection in the crafting process would help the villagers feel comfortable with their new weapon, and many young hunters would use the same bow throughout their lives. It even became a tradition for young hunters to gift a bow to their beloved as a marriage proposal. A tradition that survived into the [[Third Age]].

{{Journal entry|
The KotHaar do not die as we do. There is no afterlife for them, just silence. They are reduced to fragments of obsidian, crushed down and down with the weight of their souls. Once returned to the Elder Kiln the KotHaar will live again, it just may take some time. Fortunately, time is irrelevant to the KotHaar and they are content to simply wait out the aeons until their time comes again. So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait.

There is a common misconception that the KotHaar are a hive mind. Certainly many of them work as if they are one, but they are bound by a shared purpose, not a shared consciousness. This is a distinction that other races struggle with regularly, but it is easily understood when, as inevitably happens once in a while, one of the KotHaar turns away from their intended purpose and dares to wonder what else could be.

There are a few stories, hidden in the deserts, of KotHaar explorers found doing various things. They might spend days staring at a cactus, or they might dig through a mountainside to see what’s inside.

Perhaps this chest armour, that you now wear, might once have dreamed of being something other than its purpose. Now, perhaps, that dream has come true.
}}

The '''pharaoh's sceptre''' is a [[power level]] 7 [[staff]] that can be crafted at a [[mystic forge]]. The recipe is learned from the [[Icthlarian fetish]], the reward from the quest [[Contact!]]. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using [[ascension cores]].

Its [[special effect]] is Royal Mandate: While holding the Sceptre, the wielder is able to use the [[Confuse]] spell without consuming [[runes]]. Its special action is Sworn Servant: This summons [[Buddy]], a friendly [[kalphite]] to attack and distract enemies in combat. Buddy can be up for up to 3 minutes as long as it is still alive, and will take another five minutes for it to respawn when recasting the sceptre's special action. However, due to Hollow Vessel, while Buddy is active, the wielder regains [[stamina]] 10% slower than normal.

Although it can be nice to have a companion on the sands, Buddy can cause certain combat encounters to fail to end correctly (like the [[nightmare crucible]]s, [[fight caves]], or the fight against [[Fuzan]]) since they wait for every enemy in the arena to be killed and Buddy counts against that tally.<ref>This is a known bug (pun intended).</ref> The 25 [[astral rune]] cost for Confuse is also not very expensive, and although handy, does not provide any [[Magic]] [[XP]] from confused enemies attacking other enemies. As this staff has no other direct benefits to the user, other staves are often used over it.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
The Moon Garou tried the whole Pharaoh concept exactly once. Unused to non-violent systems of government, they gathered together as a people and pulled stones from a bag to decide who was the luckiest of all of them, and therefore who deserved to rule.

It was, as you can imagine, not a smart system of governance.

The winner was a garou called Hakanaten, and he did not want the job. He had always been an outsider, far more interested with the goings on of the nearby Kalphite hives then he was with the goings on of the city. Still, he had been chosen by an assumption of destiny and was set upon a throne with crown and sceptre in hand.

He hated it. He made decisions as best he could, but could never please everyone. If he tried to help one person, it angered another. If he cast judgement on a lawbreaker, he was deemed cruel by some and weak by others. No matter what he tried, he only found himself more and more isolated from his kin.

In the end a revolt saw him deposed and the throne destroyed. He was cast into the hive he so adored, where he was expected not to live for long. Yet, he had studied the hive and he could mimic their behaviours better than some of his own people’s. He helped them dig tunnels. He joined them on hunts. He lived a life far happier among the hive then he ever did at home.

The sceptre, that had been cast down with him, carries with it a measure of his fondness for the insects. It is said that anyone who wields it, can call on the hive for aid, in memory of an unlucky monarch.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Fashioned from clean water, weeds and animal bones, this mixture leeches out the vitality from those ingredients and transfers it to the sick and dying plants in your care. Cooked over a range, this concoction was first thought to be the domain of druids and herblore masters, but in truth it was a cook who put the pieces together. 

Old mother{{sic}} Potterington was much beloved by the people of Bramblemead. On weekends, when people allowed themselves brief breaks from their toils, she would whip up a great batch of something delicious and simmering, and neighbouring farmers would drop by for a meal.

This kindness extended not only to people, but to her garden and farming patches too. She whipped up a broth so infused with nutrients that Brassica Prime himself is said to have blessed it. When fed to plants, their withering and wilting leaves would stiffen and return to vibrancy — life and vitality theirs once again.

Now you can brew such a concoction yourself, so that your plants might always life their healthiest days.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal_entry|
There is no 'Rat Master' position in the Black Knights or Zamorakian Magi. 'Rat Master' is very-much self-appointed.

Rats would come and go through the banquet hall, the dorms and the library, and Skrexis would watch them. There was one rat - fat as a carnivorous chinchompa - that led them. One eye was scarred, and its claws were long, made for gouging. Skrexis monitored the rats' movement, noting when they would be in each room. The rats had a timetable; they were predictable.

Skrexis waited for the fat, leader rat in the kitchens. He sat, cross-legged, with a saucepan in his lap. A wave of rats poured into the kitchen, saw Skrexis and flooded back out. But the fat rat, it approached, one eye locked on the seated man.

Skrexis wished there was someone, a bard perhaps, to have seen that fight. It was for the ages. The two combatants scratched, lurched, swung and skittered, but Skrexis emerged victorious. Bloodied, he approached the rats who had been watching from the doorframe.

Skrexis had earned the title of Rat Master, by way of combat.
}}
