Saga:
{{Otheruses|major narrative arcs for the game|the list of individual quests|Quests}} '''Wiki note:''' ''The page is still missing the final chapter of Kuldra's Saga due to the page being posted during the game's early access.'' '''Sagas''' are major narrative arcs in ''[[RuneScape: Dragonwilds]]'', told through the game's primary [[quests]]. Each saga follows a central storyline that unfolds across the continent of [[Ashenfall]]. Most regions contain a single chapter dedicated to their local narrative; however, '''Wrath of Velgar''' is an exception, beginning in [[Brynmoor]] before continuing into [[Ghornfell]], making it the only chapter to span multiple regions. == Sagas == === Kuldra's Saga === '''Kuldra's Saga''' is the first saga to be released alongside ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''. It follows the [[player]]'s arrival in Ashenfall and their efforts to confront [[Kuldra]] and her [[Dragon (race)|dragons]]. It takes place during the [[Sixth Age]], following the events of {{RSL|Aftermath}}, and establishes the beginning of the player's journey across the continent of Ashenfall. ''[[The Story So Far]]'', is a [[Lore Scraps|lore scrap]] entry that provides an overview of the events preceding the start of the game. ==== Chapter 1: Wrath of Velgar ==== {{OccDur|Dragon Slayer}}
"They swooped down from the skies and decimated the landing party. Whole teams of people, gone, just like that. "Queen Kuldra bids you welcome," they laughed, as our comrades drew their final breath''.''" - ''[[Wise Old Man]]''
This is the opening chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga''', '''Wrath of Velgar'''. Upon arriving in Ashenfall, the player emerges from an ancient, ruined [[Temple of Saradomin|Saradominist temple]] and is introduced to essential survival techniques by several notable characters, including the [[Wise Old Man]], [[Doric]], [[Vannaka]], and [[Zanik]]. After completing this introductory training, the player sets out across the region of Brynmoor, battling [[Goblin (race)|goblins]] and other hostile creatures to acquire stronger equipment before confronting the dragon general [[Velgar]] at [[Velgar's Rise|his tower]] within Ghornfell. The chapter concludes with the player defeating Velgar and delivering his severed head to the Wise Old Man outside the tower. ==== Chapter 2: Beyond the Grave ==== {{OccDur|Withering Heights}}
"Welcome to Fellhollow. The whole region is infected with a terrible withering. Some dread curse that untethers the soul and drags it to the River Noumenon without ever sailing upon it, preventing the dead from moving on. This cannot stand''.''" - [[Death (Grim Reaper)|''Death'']]
'''Beyond the Grave''' is the second chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey into the region of [[Fellhollow]] after the defeat of Velgar, here the players will be introduced to Death. Here, they will learn of [[Imaru]] and the plague she had unleashed within the region centuries ago and will be asked to slay her in order to restore the region. Here the players discover the [[Wither]] effect and how to enter it, and escape it. Players will be facing all kinds of [[undead]] when in the region, even [[green dragon]]s, preparing themselves before they face Imaru. The chapter concludes with the player defeating Imaru and the delivering her severed head to Death. ==== Chapter 3: Madness of Zamorak ==== {{OccDur|Black Knight's Fortress}}
"Full of angry Zamorakians. Quite the bother. Good thing you're here though, you can get us moving again. The way is blocked by something called the Gatekeeper. Not sure what it is, or who it is, but it's in the way. There's a nasty magical barrier before we can even reach them, but Doric's working on it as we speak." - [[Wise Old Man]]
'''Madness of Zamorak''' is the third chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey to [[Dowdun Reach]] after the defeat of Imaru. Here, the player will be asked to help Doric unlike the barrier that blocked them from entering the next region. They'll have to located shards of the [[Dreaming Stone]] in order to restore it and undo the barrier. Players will be facing [[Black Knights]], [[mage of Zamorak]], [[blue dragon]]s and more in order to prepare and repair the stone and fight against the [[Black Knight Titan]]. The chapter concludes with the player's defeating the Titan and bringing his broken sword to Doric to prove their victory. ==== Chapter 4: Fire of Fuzan ==== {{OccDur|Icthlarin's Little Helper}}
''"Souls are coming to me from Umbral Sand at a faster and faster rate. My good friend Death informed me that the culprit is Fuzan, a dragon tyrant of these dunes." - [[Icthlarin]]''
'''Fire of Fuzan''' is the fourth and penultimate chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey to [[Umbral Sands]] after defeating the Black Knight Titan. Here, they will be asked by [[Icthlarin]] to assist them in rebuilding his mother's mirror to lead them into [[Fuzan]]'s lair. The player will be tasked to gain the trusts of the Moon [[Garou (race)|Garou]] in order to gain the pieces needed for the mirrors. Players will be facing [[kalphite]]s, [[red dragon|red dragons]], [[KotHaar]] and other dangers within the region to prepare for their fight against Fuzan. This chapter concludes with the player defeating Fuzan and his [[Fight Cave|trials]], as well as delivering his head to Icthlarin. ==== Chapter 5: Rage of Kuldra ==== {{OccDur}}
"''TBA''"
'''Rage of Kuldra''' is the fifth and final chapter of the '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey through the [[Scorned Wilderness]] raid after defeating Fuzan and liberating the Umbral Sands from his tyranny. == Future Sagas == It was revealed by [[Mod Dutch]] in the [[RuneFest]] reveal [https://www.twitch.tv/videos/2826225990?t=01h28m13s Twitch stream] that Kuldra's story isn't the conclusion for the story of game There are future sagas planned for the game. === Unnamed Saga === This next saga will focus on a multi-year journey to discover the ancient magic guarding the continent of Ashenfall and potentially revealing the continent to the rest of Gielinor. More information on this new saga will potentially be revealed at [[RuneFest 2026]] and closer to the [[Upcoming updates|winter update]] set to release towards the end of 2026. == Quests == {| class="wikitable lighttable" !Sagas !Quests !Region |- | rowspan="5" |'''Kuldra's Saga''' |[[Dragon Slayer]] |[[Brynmoor]]/[[Ghornfell]] |- |[[Withering Heights]] |[[Fellhollow]] |- |[[Black Knight's Fortress (Quest)|Black Knight's Fortress]] |[[Dowdun Reach]] |- |[[Icthlarin's Little Helper]] |[[Umbral Sands]] |- |[Scorned Wilderness Primary] |[[Scorned Wilderness]] |} == See Also == * [[Quests]] * [[Ashenfall]] * [[History]] == Trivia == * Originally, Beyond the grave was promoted as "Hunger of Imaru" throughout the first two [[upcoming updates]]' roadmaps. * Sagas in ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' are similar to the "quest series" in ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'' and ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}''. ** This is not to be confused with the {{RSL|Fremennik Sagas}} in ''RuneScape''.

They had harvested it from a cave near the Salve river and found ways to cultivate it on Ashenfall’s soil, by utilising the natural magic infusing everything.

Sanctified by faith and magic, this amulet was fatal to the undead, and the dragonkin [[Lacrussa]] was fascinated with the properties. She stole the recipe for its creation and hid it within her vault, long before the withering curse spread over [[Fellhollow]]. Instead she had delved too deeply in her own experiments and discovered something buried within the earth that would twist and reanimate the dead.

It is given to the [[player]]s by [[Doric]] as a reward when completing [[Seeking Salvation]]. This crystal is required for the creation of the [[salve amulet]]. Players can obtain more by buying it from [[Death (Grim Reaper)|Death]] after Seeking Salvation is completed.

==History==
According to the salve amulet's journal, the crystal was brought to [[Ashenfall]] during the [[Third Age]] by Saradominists priest, cultivating it on Ashenfall's soil by utilising the natural magic infusing everything. With the amulet having properties against the undead, the [[Dragonkin (race)|dragonkin]] [[Lacrussa]] was fascinated with it, stealing the recipe for its creation and hid it within her vault. The crystal was used when she had found something buried within the earth that would twist and reanimate the dead, before [[Fellhollow]]'s undead infection. The amulet helped her fend off against the undead from overrunning her lab, that is until she met her end by [[Kuldra]].

==Trivia==
* While it is said that a salve crystal was transported from the mainland to Ashenfall, the crystal did not receive any power until the [[Fourth Age]], when {{RSL|Lowerniel Drakan|Lord Drakan}} and his {{RSL|Vampyre (race)|vampyre army}} were sealed within {{RSL|Morytania}}. This event had water from the {{RSL|River of Salve|river of Salve}} enter the mine where the crystals deposit resided, having them infuse with the water's holy magic. Why this one had power is unknown.
** It has been confirmed by [[Mod Raven]] that this was intentional; however, it is not meant to be a lorefail, but a mystery to "why did the amulet work."{{CiteDiscord|author=Mod Raven|url=https://discord.com/channels/303835144073248770/474587164647358475/1457659608691638333|date=05 January 2026|quote=The intention here was to create an area of mystery and discussion about how these things might connect or work. Where did this practice come from? What is special about the crystals? Why did they think to do that with the Salve? Where did it all actually start? 

Lacrussa's amulet should not have worked, yet it did... why? There is an element in play that you can infer stuff from if you understand the full extent of Lacrussa's situation.|ctxquote=Aren't its powers over the undead directly derived from the River Salve blessing
In which case it being named salve is very much not a misnomer
And it wouldn't have existed in the Third Age}}

The '''scarab staff''' is an interactable staff found in the [[Manafem Plains]] Pyramid that has a safe 25-metre radius for players to walk within. Players can wield it to ward off scarabs to avoid getting damaged 2–3 [[health]] per second. However, players cannot bring the staff out of the pyramid. Wielding the staff will '''not''' allow the player to jump, so players will need to place it strategically to avoid getting damaged by the nearby scarabs.

In addition, players cannot use the staff to fight any of the [[kalphite]]s, as this will automatically place the staff on the ground and make the player re-equip their previous tools/weapons.

The scarab staff '''must''' be placed on a horizontally flat surface for it to lock in place and provide protection; otherwise, the staff will fall to the ground and will need to be picked up again.

The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate.

Lord Rasmodel's greatest challenge came from within. It did not carry a sword or crossbow.

The Shadow Knight numbers were dropping. It was impossible to resign from the order -- that was written in the charter -- but more and more of the knights were falling into madness. If it were physical wounds, Lord Rasmodel could have done something about the epidemic. He could amputate the problem with a single swing of his sword. But his enemy was intangible.

He decided to visit those on the precipice of madness. Most of them were unintelligible, but some talked of food not satisfying them anymore. Others called out to the Dreaming Stone like it was their mother, as if it would save them. In many cases, it sounds like the afflicted were arguing with themselves: two enemies unleashing an enmity.

The choice comes down to what bolt type is preferred, as the dorgeshuun can only fire [[bone bolts]].

Restraint was certainly beaten into the Black Snipers that night.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|Not all magic is focused on the obliteration of one’s enemies; though many would argue that’s where the fun lies. No, magic can also improve the rest of one’s life in similarly impressive ways.

This necklace, favoured by artisans, miners, lumberjacks and similar, is an example of such magic. The enchantment is simple, it enhances ones luck. When swinging at a rock, you have a higher chance of finding that weak seam. If cutting down a tree, the forces acting on your cuts make it easier to fell it. You are a little luckier in your endeavours and therefore get better results.

In the Wizard’s  Tower this has caused no end of arguments. Luck, isn’t a thing. It’s not a law of creation, nor a principle on which the measured universe runs. Cause has Effect. Doing one action creates an outcome, a different action another. Luck, whilst popular with the layperson, isn’t something that can be measured or refined, it’s simply coincidence, nothing more.

Yet, this necklance proves that it must be a thing. Even though it can’t be. Therefore this little trinket has been the source of some of the longest, loudest and most violent debates for decades.
}}

Skullsplitter:
{{Infobox Item |name = Skullsplitter |image = Skullsplitter.png |release = 15 April 2025 |update = RuneScape: Dragonwilds is out! |item_type = Melee Weapon |weight = 15.0 |repaircost = 1 [[bronze bar]] |description = A deadly weapon with a disturbingly accurate name. }} '''Skullsplitter''' is a [[power level]] 3 one-handed weapon that can be crafted using a [[blacksmith's bench]]. The recipe is learned by consuming the [[vestige]] [[remnants of a shattered skull]], received randomly as a drop from killing [[garou berserker]]s at a 1/50 drop rate. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension core]]s. Its [[special effect]] is +15% [[critical strike]] chance, which equates to an average 1.0375x damage increase. However, that assumes that the [[critical strike]] chance never goes over 100%, which would be wasted. Currently, the base chance is 10%, the 2/3 [[melee armour]] set bonus provides 50% after a block, and the [[lesser Attack potion]] provides 25%, equaling 85% before adding the Skullsplitter's 15%. This weapon has slightly higher base damage than the [[goblin "Swingslash"]] but slightly lower than the [[zombie axe]] at equivalent power levels. The [[zombie axe]], however, deals both crush and slash damage, making it worse against enemies weak to crush but resistant to slash (including [[skeletal hoplite]]s, [[zogre]]s, [[black knight warrior]]s, [[black knight guardian]]s, and the [[black knight titan]]). ==Journal==
{{journal entry|
Wardstones are handy tools for anyone working with wards. Armour, when created on an anima-rich continent like [[Ashenfall]], is infused with threads of enchantment that harness natural magic to provide an extra layer of protection for the wearer.

This protection depletes upon use, as the energy within the ward is expended on the effect. But the wardstone can rectify this situation… for a price.

The stone around the wardstone is hollow and more brittle than it seems, and the rune essence is carefully laid within it along with a final ingredient – a drop of the creators own blood. This blood, and the rune essence formation, creates a sort of harmonious connection between the bearer of the wardstone and the stone itself.

When the stone is broken, it activates the rune essence and draws [[anima]] in from the nearest pure source – the soul of the user.

Souls are containers of pure anima. They grow over time from experience and adventure, the more the bearer of said soul enriches their life with activity, the stronger the soul. This means that the damage the wardstone creates, whilst not insignificant, is easily repaired through the simple passage of time. Especially on Ashenfall, where merely surviving to the next hour is an adventure.

Wardstones are great in a pinch, but one must be careful not to use too many, less the damage they deal to themselves becomes too great.
}}

Smoked herring is not, as the idiom will claim, 'red'. It is more of an orange, coppery colour. That means the term 'red herring' is something of a red herring. Which tracks.

The process of smoking a herring has changed over the years. In the Second Age, a herring would be smoked in the village elder's pipe, in the hope that some of the elder's wisdom would transfer to the fish. {{Journal entry|
One of the most challenging dishes to prepare on Ashenfall is the smoked infernal eel. The whole process is an olfactory gauntlet. You are bombarded with such a succession of smells, some wonderful, some horrifying, that it can feel like sprinting through the back alleys of Varrock. Some chefs from the Cook's Guild have compared it to 'seeing one's life flash before their eyes'. Except with noses.

Complete the gauntlet, however, and the bounty is worth it. Many people call smoked infernal eel a 'delicacy' but the term doesn't really suit. Delicacy is derived from 'delicate', after all. The taste is more like a salt-chinchompa exploding under your tongue.

Something about rewriting the underpinning rules of your reality, with little more than force of will and a handful of stones, makes people reach for lofty goals. In Fellhollow it was the wizard Falistrius who wanted to make a name for herself.

She wanted to be a magical scholar. A researcher who might uncover the secrets of the universe itself. They sought spells of greater and greater power, dabbling in mysteries both profane and forbidden, and came up empty-handed.

After constantly searching for power, it was an unexpected duel that would grant her the fame she sought, at a price she would have preferred to avoid. A travelling elven sorcerer arrived in the village of Emberwood one night and the local drunk foolishly picked a fight with him. Unfortunately for Falistrius that drunk was her wife.

The elf challenged the drunk to a duel, for satisfaction over a drink spilled, and by local custom Falistrius was forced to answer. They met in the forests of Fellhollow, and unleashed their magic.

The elf’s spells were like nothing she had ever seen before. Cold and dark, sanguine and terrible, they tore into her magical defences like they were nothing and writhed inside her soul like a foul nightmare. Against the strain, her staff shattered, leaving her vulnerable. In desperation she grasped a fallen hollow tree branch and urged her magic through it.

It wasn’t enough to save her. But it was enough to earn the respect and satisfaction of the sorcerer, who left the region with his pale-skinned cohorts. Ever since then, young Fellhollow mages would craft staves from the hollow bark from the forest, in memory of Falistrius. }} ==Update history== {{UH| {{UL |type = update |date = [[23 June]] [[2026]] |ver = Eye on Ashenfall - 0.12.0 |update = * Item is now created at the Mystic Forge, as the Smithing Anvil has been removed from the game. }} {{UL |type = update |date = [[15 December]] [[2025]] |ver = Eye on Ashenfall - 0.10 |update = * Added to game. }} }} ==Trivia== * The appearance of the item closely resembles that of ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'s (RS3)'' {{RSL|Splitbark wand}}. {{Staves}} {{Weapons}}

'''Square foundations''' are [[Construction|constructed]] objects that are not required to have a roof or a stable foundation. Note that the square foundation has eight points of contact: four at the corners and four on the bottom of each vertical beam. Players can only build up to six square foundations, either stacked on top of each other or side by side, without a stable foundation in between (or at the bottom of the stack). The square foundation is 4 metres long on both sides (which includes the frame surrounding the tile).

A square foundation is not recommended for building floors in a two-floor player-built house, as the bottom legs will make it hard for players to move around the house. It may be recommended to use [[square tile]]s without legs on the bottom.

Hunting, therefore, became a very popular activity, with many competitions and events crafted to provide meals for the draconic caretakers.

When the withering began to spread and the dead began to rise, steel bolts proved just as effective at piercing a zombie’s skull, as it{{sic|should be "they"}} would catching{{sic|supposed to be "be catching"}} the quarry from a hunt. 

Though the dead would come in droves, the crossbow would let them be taken out at great distance, keeping the last remaining settlements safter{{sic|supposed to be "safer"}} for just a few days longer. Every moment counted in those final days.
}}

It created the gap between animals and people, the first step toward civilization. 

It’s also the first tool to lead to murder.

==Journal==
{{Journal_entry|
Summoner Flament's experiments were sanctioned by Alric but given a wide berth by everyone else. He was less interested in the comings and goings of demons - how to bring them into this world, how to shuffle them out - and was more concerned with demonic behaviours. He wanted to see what the average avernic demon would do in a myriad of situations: what do they do when starved? How do they behave when in the company of other, non-avernic demons? Could they drown? Could they be dropped from a great height?

Summoner Flament had a pit. It was in that pit that he would keep his testing demons. He would get an allocation from the magi (who would shuffle away before they had to interact with Flament). Alric knew that Flament's works were unorthodox but produced results that could be leveraged against the demons.

And it was from the top of the pit that Flament scratched notes, watched, and sang.

"Ten red demons, sitting in a pit. Ten red demons, sitting in a pit. And if one Black Knight should accidentally slip...

There'll be ten red demons, chewing human bits."

There was madness in Summoner Flament before the Dreaming Stone shattered.
}}

This is the truth of the [[Garou (race)|garou]] philosophy. Strength and cunning dominates all. The Garou thanes demonstrate this might in the weapons they wield. Though heavier and more tiring, this axe swings with deadly force, capable of cleaving through almost any armour.

'''Titan’s wrath''' is a [[power level]] 6 [[greatsword]] received from the quest [[Black Knight's Fortress]] and found in the [[Black Knight's Fortress reward pack]] or created using a [[blacksmith's bench]]. The recipe is learned by acquiring the [[broken Titan's Wrath]] by defeating the [[Black Knight Titan]]. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension core]]s.

This weapon has three [[special effects]]: Its [[special attack]] is called Baptism of Fire, which deals damage and applies [[Burning]] to all enemies (and the player) within a 5 meter radius. Kills with this attack trigger Burning Execution which causes the weapon to become enchanted with fire magic, and further kills refresh the effect. However, this is an Enchanted Weapon, and additional enchantments cannot be cast on this weapon, whether [[Enchant Weapon: Fire]] or [[Enchant Weapon: Air]].

This weapon has higher damage ranges than the [[shadow sword]] or other [[greatswords]], but its incompatability with [[Enchant Weapon: Air]] means it misses out on the extra damage and attack speed from that enchantment. Similarly, Baptism of Fire is certainly cool, but [[Enchant Weapon: Fire]] is far easier to proc and maintain, and the forward momentum and spin of most other greatswords special actions will be hard to pass up.

Lord Rasmodel has been put to rest at last.

He rarely knew quiet. His family pushed and cajoled him to further the Rasmodel name. Then he was beset by nightmares, as two malevolent beings grappled over his mind. When the Dreaming Stone shattered, they all took him. He was their spoils.

We can only hope that, when death came, there was quietus. He felt it for a moment as the Dreaming Stone fell, and - perhaps - he feels it on the journey over the Noumenon.

The part of him that was a titan - that part remains. You hold it in your hands. Unleash its wrath.

The '''toktz-ket-xil''' is a [[power level]] 7 [[shield]] that can be crafted at a [[blacksmith's bench]] after studying the [[unyielding obsidian construct]] [[vestige]], a 1/20 drop from [[Tok-Xil]]s. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension core]]s.

Its [[special effect]] increases [[melee]] damage after a [[parry]] by 15%. This only increases melee damage; it does not increase [[magic]] or [[ranged]] damage. This effect is more powerful than it seems though as all damage increases like this are multiplicative: With all of them active, damage done can easily '''triple'''. For more info, see [[combat]].

This shield has 6 less [[block]] than most other shields at the same [[power level]], but no damage is taken or [[stamina]] consumed with a [[parry]]. By adding this shield to all of the other damage increases, the [[adamant mace]] (for example) will deal 50 more damage every parry, with no cooldown. Compare that to the [[dragonblight shield]] at power level 7, which will do 6 [[poison]] damage per second for 15 seconds, a total of 90 damage, but only once every 20 seconds. Poison damage also does not provide [[Attack]] [[XP]].

==Journal==
{{Journal entry| [[Ulv]] was always the silent hunter, in more ways than one. While it was true that no word ever left his lips, his footsteps, breath and, most importantly, his arrows were all equally devoid of sound. [[The Wild Knights]] would jokingly call him the Silent Killer - though over time, the crueller among them called him Silent But Deadly - knowing he lacked the ability to argue back. The boy took these insults with quiet grace, never biting back, never reacting. He was used to such small cruelties, having faced them all his life.

He had carved the bow himself and once walked [[Ravanna]] through the process. The two of them had a true a friendship as could ever be hoped for. No linger romantic tensions. No transaction or debt. No honour chained them together. They were friends simply because they were. Because two lonely people had found each other and a comfort in the other's eccentricities. The wolf and the bat, platonic soulmates to the end.

For one of his birthdays, Ravanna enchanted the bow with a simple spell. She took animal bones, skulls and hides and wove necromantic magic through them, wrapping them around the limb and grip of the bow, imbuing them with just enough of the [[Underworld]] to strip them of their sound and a little of their substance. Like ghosts, the arrows would sail silently through the air, dropping targets that never knew what hit them.

It would have been the perfect birthday gift. If only Ulv had lived long enough to receive it.

The [[garou]] can be brutal in their assaults, considering notions like mercy to be the domain of the weak and cowardly. Ulv was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time. He was ambushed by a patrol of young garou looking for the bloodmark that would grant them adulthood. There were six of them; Ulv reduced their number to four before claws tore his through, silencing him forever.

When Ravanna found his body, she went mad. An anger unlike any other, a rage more powerful than any storm, waged a war of light and the dark inside her. The darkness won. Using the souls of the slain garou, Ravanna's necromantic curse tore through the Highlands, twisting the clouds into screaming things filled with a mere sliver of her rage. AS the ghosts of the dead garou crashed about within them, the clouds unleashed lightning and thunder upon the populace below, destroying countless settlements in an instant and countless more over the centuries that followed.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Named after Victoria Thistlethwaite, of Bramblemead, this cake has been popular at the most lavish of parties across the region. Victoria was a well-regarded chef, but one whose culinary obsessions lay only with the sweetest of treats. She would craft biscuits, pastries and candied treats of such quality, that even Bandos once visited her little cafe to try one.

So moved was the god of war by her delicious pastries, that he left three goblins to watch over her as the war against the garou began, and those goblins would defend her with their lives. Unfortunately, goblin lives are surprisingly fleeting at the best of times, and in an actual war they lasted perhaps no more than a few hours. Victoria's little shop was consumed in a terrible inferno, reducing all her sweetest of treats to little more then motes of blackened ash, whisked away in the wind.

In honour of Bandos, and the bond that was struck with this mortal chef, goblins of Ashenfall pass down this cake recipe from generation to generation, in the hope that all might share in the deliciousness.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
The blade is not just a weapon in the wilds of Ashenfall, it’s a tool. Sometimes it’s the difference between seeing tomorrow and having a very bad today. 

Dwarves have always understood the importance of properly maintaining one’s equipment. They turned the care for their weapons into a ritual of almost religious significance. Blades would be cleaned, serviced and sharpened so that they might cut through deadlier dangers and challenge greater threats.

The whetstone is a simple device, but one that served as a backbone of this ritual. A smith would learn to gently sharpen the blade to the thinnest edge possible, treating it almost like a competition. They would boast and brag with each other about the sharpness of their blades. 

A popular dwarven myth speaks of the Prime Whetstone, capable of sharpening a blade to the point that no armour or metal could withstand it. Sadly, or perhaps thankfully, no evidence exists to provide any truth to the myth.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
It is said these swamps are haunted. Those who wander it at night, tell stories of whispering that bubbles up from the fetid water.

There is a coldness to these swamps, that is more than just temperature. It reaches beneath the warmest clothing and presses itself into bone and blood. Heartbeats slow and bravery breaks beneath its touch.

The trees here are old and spiteful, their roots wrapped around the bones of adventurers, villagers, and warriors alike. They care not for goblin, human, or [[Garou (race)|garou]], they will strangle the remains of any within their reach.

Occasionally tiny stones will bubble from the surface, black as midnight and cold as the darkest winter night. A villager once tried to craft jewelry from these stones, thinking them beautiful. It took twelve village guard to put an end to her murder spree.

This cape is woven from the fibres of swamp plants, and shields its wearer from the swamp’s whispers. Or so the old wives tales claim.
}}

{{Journal entry|
Trapped by a shrine that stood atop a rocky island, surrounded by the hungry dead, Sir Lateef prayed to Saradomin with all his strength. He begged for salvation, for a miracle that might free him, but silence was his only answer. He barricaded himself atop the monument, the dead scrabbling at his defences, their unholy growling keeping him from even a moment’s sleep. As time drew on, and hunger and thirst took him, he turned to the symbol of Saradomin in defeated rage. Where was his god? Why was he abandoned? Had he not spent his life in service of the lord of light? Enraged, he took his sword and cleaved Saradomin’s symbol from its plinth, causing it to crash to the floor. Filled with guilt, he hid the fallen piece from his sight. His last act was one of blasphemy, but perhaps an act justly performed.
}}

{{Journal entry| Ulv had many skills, but hunting was his strongest. He was inherently quiet, still as the night, and he could hold his position, in the trees or bushes, for hours at a time. Ravanna was never good at this. When the two of them hunted together, Ravanna would sneeze, cough, or scream at the sight of an unexpected insect, and the two of them would watch their quarry disappear off into the night.

Although this would occasionally test their friendship, Ulv never really held it against Ravanna. Instead, he continued attempting to teach the necromancer the ways of the forest, and the techniques the Wild Knights would use to track down game. It never took. Try as she might, Ravanna was never going to be silent as a shadow.

In apology, she looked for a way to create a weapon that would reduce the impact of her noisy nature. Longbows fired further and faster, meaning that less stealth was needed. She made her way into Fellhollow in search of a material strong enough, and returned with willow branches that she crafted into a longbow as a gift for her friend.

Their hunts improved dramatically afterward. That was, until they became the hunted. 
}}

{{journal entry|
Druids dislike violence but understand its place. The natural world is full of blood, murder and death. The strong consume the weak. Predator against prey. This they understand, though they seldom like it. When they must resort to violence, they choose the simple approach. Man’s strength comes not from their muscles but from their creativity and ingenuity. Just as a wolf has claws, a hunter has a bow.

When a bow must be drawn, the druids prefer arrows made of simple wood. Gathered twigs and branches, whittled down to sharp points. They see it as the forest giving them the blessing to go on the hunt. Traditionally, feathers are gathered from around the forest floor, taken when dropped or from a bird’s moulting. This keeps the number of arrows low, forcing a hunter to be accurate and precise, lest they run out of chances.

Thus, death is swift at the hands of a bow, and balance isn’t damaged. This the druids preached to the villagers.

In the village of Bramblemead, children grew up knowing battle. The God Wars hadn't reached them yet, but the priests always knew that danger was coming. So children were taught combat in the form of a game.

Carpenters were encouraged to make little wooden swords so that the children could emulate the noble paladins who wandered the village. These soldiers were held up as role models. Young men and women daydreamed through school of taking up those glittering swords and running off into adventure.

These weapons clicked and clacked against one another, seemingly harmless to the adults that watched. But wood in Bramblemead was hardened and preserved by druidic magic, and the damage these swords could deal soom became clear. Injuries were common, bruises and broken bones were the rite of passage of every child.

It was fortunate, perhaps, that these weapons were so painful — because the children of Bramblemead grew up with a better understanding that war was no game.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
The hunter is the lifeblood of the Moon Garou. The Umbral Sands are not as hospitable to agriculture as many would like, so diets must be supplemented with fresh meat. This is particularly true for the Moon Garou, who remain primarily carnivorous in nature.

One hunter, Flytr, was the first to craft a longbow from the yew trees in the oases. Legend had it that the trees were sacred, special, a gift of the River Mother, designed to keep the Moon Garou safe. It was the greatest of blasphemies to use the wood for anything, but Flytr had never been particularly concerned with matters of faith.

She found a tree that had been struck by lightning, to lessen the guilt of repurposing the wood. She whittled down branch and bough, to create the longbow and, when she was done, she could have sworn the weapon was excited to be used.

It felled foes at great range, making her one of the best hunters the tribe had ever seen. Soon after, yew trees were no longer protected, as it came to be believed that the strength of the bow was proof that the River Mother wanted the wood to be used.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Let us dwell, for a moment, on the original owner of this club, a man named Mort. Mortimer Grimm had the sort of name adored by those who believe in nominative determinism. Mort Grimm, his parents effectively cursed him at birth to become an undead monstrosity, and their curse came true.

The undead were rare in Ghornfell, but not unheard of. Some druids, who spent too long in the Whispering Swamps, apparently learned strange rituals that would raise a corpse as a mindless servant, doomed to wander the world in search of delicious, delicious brains. Mort was one of these, though he resurrected with somewhat less all-consuming-hunger than his cohorts. As the other zombies were herded towards human encampments, Mort wandered off into the poisonous Bloodblight Swamp, in search of mysteries. There he encountered a strange scientist who did not immediately attempt to set him on fire –  an improvement over the response from most people.

This would begin a truer friendship than Mort thought possible. Whilst, yes, the scientist could never remember Mort's name and insisted on calling him Igor. And, yes, Mort would spend much of his time listening to lectures on why everyone else is stupid, whilst carrying large and disturbingly-shaped bags of unknown contents, for the scientist. Still, they would laugh and they would watch the sunsets together, and for the first time in a long time, Mort was happy.

Until the scientist asked Mort to build the lightning conductor. One flash of inspiration later,  and Mort's tragic existence reduced itself to this somewhat sinister club.

Still, waste not want not, I always say.
}}

The '''zombie axe''' is a [[power level]] 5 one-handed [[melee weapon]] that can be crafted at a [[blacksmith's bench]]. The axe and its recipe are received by completing [[Doric's Quest]]. It can be ascended at the [[mystic forge]] using [[ascension core]]s.

Its [[special effect]] is that it deals both crush and slash damage simultaneously. Both damage types are taken into account when considering [[monsters]]' weaknesses and resistances. This weapon is effective against enemies that are weak to crush but '''not resistant''' to slash (including [[vault guardians]], [[putrid rat]]s, [[garou thane]]s, [[skeletal marauder]]s, and [[skeletal necromancer]]s). However, against enemies that are weak to crush but '''resistant''' to slash damage (including [[skeletal hoplite]]s, [[zogre]]s, [[black knight guardian]]s, [[black knight warrior]]s, and the [[black knight titan]]), this weapon will deal slightly less damage to them because resistances lower damage (-33%) more than weaknesses increase it (+25%). Note that this damage is additive rather than multiplicative, unlike other damage modifiers (i.e. it will lower damage by a factor of 0.92 rather than 0.8375).

This weapon has a higher base damage than other similar one-handed crush weapons, but that benefit is lost against enemies that are also resistant to slash, making [[Skullsplitter]] with its +15% [[critical strike]] chance more valuable. This weapon also uses the mace moveset, which hits slower than the sword, scimitar, or whip move set, therefore against enemies that are weak to slash but not resistant to crush (including [[abyssal demon]]s, [[lost soul]]s, [[zombie]]s, [[Zamorakian acolyte]]s, and [[Mage of Zamorak|mages of zamorak]]), weapons like the [[black sword]], [[Imaru's talon]], or [[abyssal whip]] may be better choices.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|[[Captain Artorius Flamhanger]] was a brave man, who stood against the rampaging forces of the damned even as his defences crumbles around him. He never wavered, never faltered, and never left a man behind.

In a better world, there would be songs about him. But [[Fellhollow]] scorns legacy, leaving only ruins and despair where hope might take root.

He held the line against the encroaching horde far longer than anywhere else in the region. Days turned into months and months grew into years. As the rest of the region vanished into death, despair and rot, Captain Flamhanger stood strong. As his children died and rose again, the captain returned them to the earth with sombre compassion. when his wife joined them in death, he gave her a final kiss of polished silver that cleaved her head from her shoulder.

In a better world he might have held back the darkness, stood as a single ray of light in a world of shadow. But this is not our world. There are no sages of this man, no great texts telling of his heroic deeds. The only sound he made in the time after his death, is the bubbling song of digestive acids within a [[zogre]]'s belly.

History is penned by the survivors and the victors, yet the deeds of the dead echo across time. This axe, simple as it may appear, is infused with vengeance against the dead that had taken so much from a good man.}}
